payload.rationale: The contract requires the 2026 GISS LOTI annual value to exceed both 1.19 (2025) and 1.28°C, so effectively ≥1.29 after GISS's two-decimal rounding. Observed Jan–Aug 2026 monthlies (1.09, 1.25, 1.32, 1.17, 1.13, 1.18, 1.25, 1.40) sum to 9.79 (mean 1.22). To reach ~1.285 unrounded, Sep–Dec must average roughly 1.41°C. Only one month so far (Aug, 1.40) is near that level, so the outcome hinges on a sharp late-year acceleration. Supporting that: NOAA CPC (10 Sep 2026) reports El Niño strengthening with >90% chance of a very strong event, eastern Pacific anomalies already >+3.0°C, and the Jul→Aug jump (1.25→1.40) is consistent with an El Niño-driven surge. The closest analog, 2023 (La Niña early, strong El Niño developing), saw GISS jump from ~1.19 in Aug to a Sep–Dec mean of ~1.40; 2026 is running ~0.15–0.2°C warmer than 2023 in comparable months, so a Sep–Dec mean of 1.45–1.55 is plausible, which would clear the threshold with margin. Too high if: Aug 1.40 is a noisy outlier, the atmosphere lags the ocean so the global response arrives mostly in early 2027 (as in 2015–16), or GISS revisions trim monthlies; a Sep–Dec mean of 1.30–1.38 would fail. Too low if: the El Niño is stronger than 2023's and late-2026 months reach 1.5+, making YES nearly certain. Net: moderately favored, ~0.7.
limitations: Four months of 2026 data are missing; annual outcome depends on Sep–Dec anomalies averaging ~1.41°C, above all but one observed month.
No fitted predictive distribution or ENSO-to-GISTEMP transfer model supplied; analog reasoning (2023, 2015) from memory.
GISS monthly values are revised; 2025 and 2024 annual values cited (1.19, 1.29) may differ from earlier releases, though the contract threshold is fixed at 1.28.
Packet is small and coordinator-selected; ENSO discussion excerpts are truncated.
